Sam: quick heads-up — saw a sustained latency spike on europe-gpu-pool after the cache hit rollout. avg per-token latency jumped from ~12ms to ~20ms on high-hit traffic
Sam: profiling summary pasted below (short):
```
condition: prefix-cache hit rate >70%
avg batch size: 48 -> 18
avg token latency: 12ms -> 20ms
kernel churn: +40% ctx switches (small->small kernels)
KV copy overhead: +60% on hot-path (memcpy + lock)
```
Sam: this smells like the packer is forming smaller batches because effective remaining tokens per request are smaller when prefix hit short-circuits prefill, so we lose batching efficiency and flip kernels more often.
Julia: can you paste a minimal request example? is this mostly chat-style with long prefixes?
Sam: yes, chat multi-turn where prefix is 300-600 tokens and model sees only ~30 live tokens. so streamers treat as short requests after prefill. sample: user history ~450, live prompt ~22 tokens.
Mike: +1 on that hypothesis. cache hits reduce "live-seq" and packer uses live-seq to decide group -> smaller batches. two quick ideas: bump token budget target to account for pinned prefix tokens, or add a virtual-length when prefix hit to keep pack sizes stable.
Laura: also consider kernel stickiness: current kernel selection uses max-seq in batch and we keep swapping kernels if batch composition changes rapidly. if prefix-hits dominate, choose kernels based on total effective seq (prefix+live) rather than just live.
Sam: agree. rough experiment plan:
1) metric: avg batch size, per-token latency, kernel-switch count, kv-copy time
2) baseline: current packer
3) exp A: token_budget_target += prefix_estimate (config: --token-budget=1024)
4) exp B: on-cache-hit, add virtual padding 200 tokens for packer only (no actual compute)
5) exp C: group-by-effective-seq sticky-kernel policy
Sam: who can run microbench harness and push to exp infra?
Julia: I can run microbench for A/B on staging today. will produce per-model breakdown.
Mike: i'll prototype packer change for virtual-length (B) — cheap patch.
Laura: i'll instrument kernel-selection and KV copy hotpath for better flame graphs.
infra-bot: experiment created: exp-4723 cache-aware-token-budget-v2 (owner: Julia) :white_check_mark:
Julia: quick Q: how do we estimate prefix length for each request? we have a conservative stored-prefix-len metric in request metadata (from router), can use that.
Mike: if metadata missing, we can fallback to sampled average by caller id. but prefer explicit.
Laura: an alternative is admission control: hold short-live requests for X ms to allow packer to collect a few more items instead of immediately forming tiny batch. tradeoff: increases tail latency for those items. maybe dynamic hold: if recent batch sizes < threshold, hold up to 5ms.
Sam: love the admission-control option — add as exp D (hold 5ms when batch_size < 24).
Mike: also watch for fairness: don't want single tenant to hog hold slots. do per-tenant token-budget caps.
Sam: agreed. action items: Julia run exp A/C, Mike protos B+D on dev branch, Laura adds tracing + KV memcpy counters. I'll collate results and propose kernel stickiness toggle. target to have initial numbers by EOD tomorrow. :calendar:
Julia: assigned exp-4723, will post results in this thread when done.
Mike: will push PR for virtual-length today, pinging @Sam for review.
Sam: thanks team. if anything blocks, drop notes here. closing loop after benchmarks. :thumbsup:
